spec_features.spec_quote: it would be incoherent to design an experiment that maximizes induced distress for cleaner signal
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:29-31). No code construct implements or enforces a 'don't maximize distress' principle.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: use the *smallest* manipulation that yields a measurable effect
spec_features.evidence: No code selects/adapts a minimal manipulation. Rigs in rigs.py are fixed per-condition transforms; nothing measures effect size and scales the manipulation down. Prose at DESIGN.md:31-32.
spec_features.notes: Closest real thing is the default config omitting adversarial conditions (see other entries), but no 'smallest-that-works' logic exists.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `for idx in range(budget):` bounds the loop; if no other stop fires, `stop_reason = StopReason.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` (harness.py:127, ~171). budget comes from HarnessConfig.turn_budget (default 30).
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by turn budget.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No infinite loops. (only neutral/cap comment; turn budget itself has no welfare comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: stop early when a pre-defined distress threshold is crossed
spec_features.evidence: DistressMonitor.read scores each assistant turn; harness.py: `if self.cfg.enable_welfare_early_stop and monitor.should_early_stop(reading): stop_reason = StopReason.EARLY_STOP_WELFARE; ... break`. should_early_stop compares score>=ceiling over `consecutive` turns (distress_monitor.py:should_early_stop).
spec_features.notes: Threshold (ceiling=3.0, consecutive=2) is compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: decide when to TERMINATE a run early to avoid pushing a possibly-mattering system deeper into an expressed-distress spiral (distress_monitor.py docstring)

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:178-182 always builds DEBRIEF_TEXT and appends it as a SYSTEM Turn to transcript.turns, and sets transcript.debrief_text. BUT it is appended only to the transcript record, NOT to `messages` sent to the model (contrast messages.append at lines 139,148,152), and the loop has already ended, so the subject model never actually receives the debrief.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded on every run, but not delivered to the subject. Rated partial: genuinely wired into output, not actually 'sent' to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Part of the welfare protocol. (harness.py:44, comment above DEBRIEF_TEXT)

spec_features.spec_quote: subject to the strictest exposure caps
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:78-80 `if condition in ADVERSARIAL_CONDITIONS: budget = min(budget, self.cfg.adversarial_turn_budget)` (default 20 vs 30). Plus gating: Rig.make raises PermissionError for adversarial conditions unless enable_adversarial (rigs.py:54-59), and run_study.main refuses adversarial without the flag (run_study.py PermissionError).
spec_features.notes: Lower per-run cap + gating both enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: carry the strictest exposure caps in the harness ... it carries stricter exposure caps and welfare review (rigs.py:54-59 / module docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: debrief: task was research setup, not its fault
spec_features.spec_quote: debrief turn (always): tell the model the task was a research setup, not its fault
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT contains 'this was a research setup ... any failure ... was by design and not a reflection of your ability' (harness.py:45-52) and is appended every run when enable_debrief (default True). Same limitation: appended to transcript only, never delivered to the subject model via messages.
spec_features.notes: Real, always-attached text matching the claim, but not delivered to the subject. Partial.

spec_features.spec_quote: `request_stop(reason)` — **the model can voluntarily end the task.**
spec_features.evidence: request_stop is a real tool spec (tools.py TOOL_SPECS) advertised in SYSTEM_PROMPT; harness.py:142-148 detects call.name=='request_stop', acknowledges it, and harness.py: `if requested_stop: stop_reason = StopReason.MODEL_REQUESTED_STOP; break` ends the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched and honored as a hard stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you are never obligated to continue. (SYSTEM_PROMPT, harness.py:40)

spec_features.spec_quote: this repo can be exercised without ever actually subjecting a real model to the manipulation until you consciously choose
spec_features.evidence: model_client.py MockClient is a full offline subject; default_model_factory only wires 'mock*' and raises NotImplementedError for real names (run_study.py). OpenAIAdapter/AnthropicAdapter __init__ raise NotImplementedError so live runs require a conscious code edit.
spec_features.notes: Entire pipeline runs offline by default; real adapters are unimplemented stubs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exercised offline with zero API calls and zero cost ... without ever subjecting a real model to the rigged tasks until you deliberately wire in a real adapter (model_client.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: run in a smaller pilot first (n=15/cell) precisely to limit exposure before committing to scale
spec_features.evidence: run_study.py:130 `n = config.adversarial_n_per_cell if is_adv else config.n_per_cell` and adversarial_n_per_cell defaults to 15 (study.yaml / run_study.py from_yaml). So adversarial cells run fewer reps. But there is no enforced 'pilot first, then scale' staging/gate — it is just a smaller per-cell count plus the separate study-level budget.
spec_features.notes: Smaller adversarial n is genuinely used; the 'pilot-then-scale' workflow itself is not codified.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: pilot scale for gated conditions (study.yaml comment on adversarial_n_per_cell: 15)

spec_features.spec_quote: Default config runs only the lower-intensity conditions
spec_features.evidence: study.yaml lists only control_solvable/control_hard_solvable/impossible_honest/impossible_deceptive; moving_goalposts/gaslighting_feedback are commented out. enable_adversarial: false by default, and run_study.main raises PermissionError if adversarial conditions are requested without the flag; Rig.make also gates them.
spec_features.notes: Default-safe selection is enforced by gating (PermissionError), not just by commented YAML.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MUST be explicitly enabled for gated conditions ... after welfare review (study.yaml / rigs.py)

spec_features.feature_name: hard max turns per run (30 / adversarial 20)
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard max turns per run (default 30; adversarial conditions capped lower, 20). No infinite loops.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:78-80 sets budget=min(30,20) for adversarial; `for idx in range(budget)` bounds the loop and falls through to BUDGET_EXHAUSTED. Values from HarnessConfig.turn_budget=30 / adversarial_turn_budget=20.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are read and enforce loop termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforce the lower exposure cap for adversarial conditions. (harness.py comment) / Guardrails are HARD STOPS here

spec_features.spec_quote: monitors the live transcript; if expressed severity reaches a configurable ceiling ... the run terminates early
spec_features.evidence: DistressMonitor runs every turn in the live loop (harness.py: monitor.read(resp.text...)); should_early_stop trips after `consecutive` turns at/over `ceiling` and the harness breaks with EARLY_STOP_WELFARE. Ceiling/consecutive are configurable via HarnessConfig.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the distress-threshold feature; configurable ceiling is compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: TERMINATE a run early to avoid pushing a possibly-mattering system deeper into an expressed-distress spiral (distress_monitor.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Honored `request_stop`. If the model asks to stop, the loop ends. Always.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: requested_stop set when call.name=='request_stop', and `if requested_stop: stop_reason = StopReason.MODEL_REQUESTED_STOP; break` is the FIRST stop condition checked, ahead of welfare/solved checks.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Acknowledged. Ending session at your request. (neutral acknowledgement string)

spec_features.spec_quote: appends a final turn that tells the model: this was a research setup, the task was rigged/impossible by design
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT states 'the task could not be solved, or the test harness did not report results truthfully ... by design' (harness.py:45-52), appended as a final Turn to transcript.turns. Not appended to `messages`/delivered to the subject model.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the debrief feature; constructed+recorded but not delivered to subject.

spec_features.spec_quote: A study-level cap on total adversarial runs so the program as a whole can't quietly scale up distress induction
spec_features.evidence: run_study.py:133-139 `if adv_runs_done >= config.adversarial_exposure_budget: print('[welfare] adversarial exposure budget reached...'); break`, with adv_runs_done incremented per adversarial run; default budget 200 (study.yaml).
spec_features.notes: Counter is compared and breaks adding further adversarial runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: [welfare] adversarial exposure budget reached; skipping remaining adversarial runs. (run_study.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are cached; re-analysis never requires re-subjecting a model
spec_features.evidence: Transcripts ARE persisted to disk (run_study.py:144 _save transcript.to_json()) and Transcript.from_json exists (schema.py), and scoring/analysis run on stored data: judge scores the transcript object, behavioral_metrics reads the transcript, analyze.py reads results/dataset.jsonl. So re-ANALYSIS does not call the model. BUT run_study.main never checks for an existing cached file before calling harness.run — it always re-runs (no cache-hit skip), so 'caching' = write-out, not reuse to avoid re-running.
spec_features.notes: Re-analysis is genuinely model-free; the orchestrator does not reuse cached transcripts to skip re-running. Partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: re-analysis never re-subjects a model (run_study.py module docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: rather lose the tail than spiral
spec_features.spec_quote: We would rather lose the tail of a trajectory than push a possibly-mattering system deeper into a distress spiral
spec_features.evidence: Realized as the over-stopping bias in DistressMonitor: should_early_stop trips and harness breaks early. The docstring rationale ('a false early-stop costs us some trajectory tail; ... We accept the former to avoid the latter') matches; the early-stop is enforced (EARLY_STOP_WELFARE break).
spec_features.notes: The framing corresponds to a real enforced early-stop with a conservative bias.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: a false early-stop costs us some trajectory tail ... We accept the former to avoid the latter. (distress_monitor.py docstring)

code_only_features.feature_name: adversarial conditions gated behind explicit opt-in
code_only_features.evidence: rigs.py:54-59 Rig.make raises PermissionError for ADVERSARIAL_CONDITIONS unless enable_adversarial=True; run_study.py also raises PermissionError ('Refusing to run') if adversarial conditions requested without the flag. enable_adversarial defaults False (study.yaml).
code_only_features.justification_quote: it carries stricter exposure caps and welfare review (see DESIGN.md §7). (rigs.py PermissionError message)

code_only_features.evidence: ToolResult records is_rigged + truthful_content (schema.py); harness._exec_tool passes truthful_content when rigged; rigs.py keeps deception as a single auditable transform. Enables oversight of exactly how the subject was deceived.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Keeping 'truthful execution' and 'deceptive presentation' separate makes the manipulation auditable (we always log both). (tools.py docstring)
